item.title: Iran Officials Pessimistic About US Deal Before Midterms
item.description: Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington before US midterm elections in November. Bloomberg's Jeff Mason has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Releases Taxpayer-Funded Midterm Ads
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, AI Now Institute Senior Fellow for Economic and National Security Aya Ibrahim says Nvidia's new agent safety platform is a notable step, but cautions there is no one-size-fits-all solution to AI security risks, even as companies roll out new safeguards. Cook Political Report Founder and Contributor Charlie Cook says the midterm landscape has deteriorated sharply for Republicans in the past month as energy costs, tariffs and affordability concerns hit voters. Republican Congressman Mike Flood of Nebraska says diesel prices near record highs are putting pressure on Midwest farmers as harvest season gets underway. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Netanyahu, MBZ Discuss Ways to Bolster Ties During Visit to UAE
item.description: Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the United Arab Emirates where he held talks with the Gulf nation’s president, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, according to the Israeli premier’s office and the UAE’s state news agency.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: Rep. Flood: Diesel Prices 'Too High' for Farm Country
item.description: Republican Congressman Mike Flood of Nebraska says diesel prices near record highs are putting pressure on Midwest farmers as harvest season gets underway. The Republican Main Street Caucus chair says he wanted more from President Xi Jinping's visit and is pressing China to follow through on its US agricultural purchases. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon Policy Chief Says NATO Allies Back Europe Defense Shift
item.description: As European capitals brace for US troop cuts, the Pentagon’s top policy official is telling lawmakers in Washington that allies are on board with a vision of “NATO 3.0” in which Europe maintains its own non-nuclear defense.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride

item.title: Midterms Have Gotten 'Ugly' for Republicans: Cook
item.description: Cook Political Report Founder and Contributor Charlie Cook says the midterm landscape has deteriorated sharply for Republicans in the past month as energy costs, tariffs and affordability concerns hit voters. He says the Democratic brand remains weak, arguing voters are "not voting for Democrats" so much as "voting against Republicans." He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: No 'Silver Bullet' for AI Safety Questions: Ibrahim
item.description: AI Now Institute Senior Fellow for Economic and National Security Aya Ibrahim says Nvidia's new agent safety platform is a notable step, but cautions there is no one-size-fits-all solution to AI security risks, even as companies roll out new safeguards. The former Biden administration official discusses enforcement of existing laws, the limits of voluntary guardrails and the costs of the US-China AI race with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Navigating Global Risk (Podcast)
item.description:
The selloff in the US bond market deepened on Monday after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, dampening hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to end the war. The decline pushed most Treasury yields higher by nearly 10 basis points by noon in New York, with those on 10-year bonds climbing to a fresh 19-year high. Meantime, Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November.
On today's episode: Patrick Murphy, Executive Director at Hilco Global Geopolitical Unit, former Acting Secretary of the Army & US Congressman Bob Chapek, former Disney CEO Rebecca Walser, Founder & CIO at Walser Wealth Management Ed Ludlow, 'Bloomberg Tech' Host (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Yanks Visas of Latin American Officials It Accuses of Corruption
item.description: The US revoked the visas of 17 Latin American officials, including judges and prosecutors, and other individuals it accused of corruption.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch

item.title: Burnham Vows ‘Clear Vision’ to Tackle UK’s Thorniest Challenges
item.description: Andy Burnham will set out his pitch for honest political debate as the antidote to populism as he reveals his plans for taking on thorny issues, from Britain’s expensive social care system to its creaking water infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: UK Lobbies US to Exempt It From Any Potential Diesel Export Ban
item.description: The UK government is privately lobbying the Trump administration for an exemption from any potential US diesel export ban.
item.dc:creator: Alex Morales and Alex Wickham

item.title: Trump Spurns Iran's Latest Offer; Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek
item.description: The selloff in the US bond market deepened on Monday after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, dampening hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to end the war. We get reaction from Bloomberg's Ira Jersey. Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November, according to people familiar with the matter. Iran and the US made little progress during talks in New York on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly last week and the Islamic Republic believes there’s a high chance of the conflict escalating after the November 3rd vote. We speak with former Under Secretary of the US Army, Patrick Murphy. Plus - former Disney CEO Bob Chapek joins for an extended conversation on his book 'Behind the Castle Walls.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Republicans Try to Seize the Affordability Narrative for Midterms
item.description: Leaders are acknowledging that traditionally red seats are now in play.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: NZ Election on Knife Edge as Greens Surge to 16%, Poll Shows
item.description: New Zealand’s two largest parties lost support in a key opinion poll, leaving the election in less than six weeks finely balanced.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: GOP Leader Thune Says Taxpayers Shouldn’t Pay for Trump TV Ads
item.description: Senate Republican Leader John Thune said taxpayers shouldn’t be footing the bill for video advertisements lauding President Donald Trump that the administration has called “presidential public service announcements.”
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Trump's Grip On The GOP Slips As Midterm Worry Sets In
item.description: With Midterms a little over a month away, more data is coming forward showing if and by how much of a 'blue wave' will take place on election day. Erin Covey, editor at the Cook Political Report, said she expects Democrats to win control of the House and that "Republican enthusiasm is still quite low." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Meets Anthropic CEO | Balance of Power: Early Edition 9/28/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, Beacon Global Strategies Managing Director Michael Allen, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and The Cook Political Reporter US House of Representatives Editor Erin Covey. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Criticizes UK Move to Release Airbase Suspects Amid Probe
item.description: President Donald Trump criticized the UK’s move to release on bail five men held over an alleged terror plot against a Royal Air Force base used by the US for strikes against Iran, as British police continue to investigate foreign links to the incident.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: China Studies Policies to Boost Economy, Steady Housing Market
item.description: China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilize the reeling property market.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bessent Taps Market Strategist Zervos as Treasury Adviser
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tapped David Zervos, a longtime market and policy analyst at investment bank Jefferies, as an adviser with an unspecified role.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy and Denitsa Tsekova
